sentences.text: JUDGMENT

This petition is filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from respondents on account of death of Mohammed Imran, husband of petitioner No.1 and 5, father of petitioner No.2 and 6 and son of petitioner No.3 and 4, in Road Traffic Accident.

2. In brief, petition averments are; That, on 08-03-2018 at about 4.15 p.m., Mohammed Imran was proceeding as pillion rider on motorcycle, bearing No.KA-51-EH-3911 which was ridden by Sulthan Ahmed Khan carefully by following all traffic rules and regulations on H. Siddaiah road, Wilson Garden, Bengaluru, when they reached near K.H. Junction at that time driver of car, bearing No.KA-51-ML-0963 came with high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle.
Due to the impact, they fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over their body.
Immediately after the accident they were shifted to Agadi 4 (SCCH-16) MVC 7880/2018 Hospital.

Thereafter, Mohammed Imran was shifted to Apollo Hospital, Jayanagar, wherein he took treatment in an intensive care, but during the course of treatment he succumbed to the injuries on 12-03-2018 at about 9.30 p.m. Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as Plumbing Contractor and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
But, on account of his untimely death petitioners lost the dependency, love and affection.
Hence, this petition for compensation.

3. In brief, the objections by respondent No.1 and 2 are that;
3(a).

In written statement of objections, respondent No.1 denied the petition averments generally and contended that Mrs. Ateeba Sultana along with her daughter Miss. Ruzaian Shaik have filed MVC 6195/2018 for claiming compensation on the death of Mr. Mohammed Imran and the said case is pending before this Tribunal, the alleged present petitioners are also claiming as legal heirs of the deceased and filed the present petitioner by suppressing the earlier case in MVC 6195/2018,
the deceased along with his father-in- law/rider of motorcycle came in rash and negligently, crossing the red light sign without observing the traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the car,
there is no negligence on the part of driver of car, the accident occurred purely due to the negligent riding of the deceased's father-in-law, car bearing No.KA-51-ML- 0963 was insured with respondent No.2 and insurance 5 (SCCH-16) MVC 7880/2018 policy was in force as on the date of accident

,
driver was having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.
He prayed for dismissal of the petition.

3(b). Respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car, bearing No.KA-51-ML- 0963 and its validity as on the date of accident, denied the petition averments generally and contended that the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Section 134(C) and 158(6) of MV Act.

Without prejudice, it contended that the alleged accident occurred only due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle, bearing No.KA-51-EH-3911, who was riding the same without holding proper driving licence and without following traffic rules and regulations came to the wrong side and he himself dashed against the car and there is no negligence Mrs. M. 3 on the part of driver of car, the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary party such as owner and insurer of vehicle, bearing No.KA-51- EH-3911 are also necessary parties to the proceedings and driver of car was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of alleged accident.

For the above denials and contentions it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. Based on the pleadings the following issues came to be framed:
6 (SCCH-16) MVC 7880/2018 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Mohammed Imran?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that Mohammed Imran was died on account of road traffic accident took place at K.H. Road, near K.H. Junction, Wilson Garden,
Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of car, bearing No.KA- 51-ML-0963 dated 08-03-2018 at about 4.15 p.m.?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
4.
What order or Award?
5. In proof of the petition averments, petitioner No.1 and 5 got themselves examined as PW1 and PW2 and marked 15 documents in Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.
Respondents did not lead their evidencce.
6. Heard the counsel for respondent No.2.
No arguments by petitioners and respondent No.1.

Perused the pleadings and evidences, on the basis, findings on the issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative 7 (SCCH-16) MVC 7880/2018 Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following REASONS ISSUE No.1 & 2:
7.
Petitioners have led their oral as well as documentary evidences.
This is a summary proceedings, so, a sum and substance of the pleadings and evidences are only emphasized.
The petitioners need to prove this issue on preponderance of probability as test for proof is preponderance of probability herein.
Respondents disputed the negligence, the incident, involvement of vehicles, injuries and death are not in dispute.

9.

The final report shows the negligence on the part of driver of the offended car.
The MVA Report reveals that there was no mechanical defects in the vehicles.
The postmortem report shows the cause of death was due to coma as a result of intra cerebral hemorrhage consequent upon trauma sustained.

9 (SCCH-16)
MVC 7880/2018 According to the MVA report there was no mechanical defects in the vehicles in the sense the incident was due to the negligence only.
No eyewitness is examined herein.
Nothing is elicited from PW's in their cross- examination by respondents and also nothing is established by respondents regarding the negligence.
Here being no contrary evidence by respondents, here is no impediment to believe the police documents regarding the negligence.
The police documents give right impression that due to the rash and negligent of driver of the car the incident occurred.

Thus,
the police records are considered.

11. Regarding objections by respondent No.2 as to non compliance of provision under Section 134(c)
and 158(6) of MV Act is concerned as the petition reached its finality and the petitioners approached the Tribunal, respondent No.2 had already taken all the contentions of respondent No.1 and respondent No.1 filed his written statement the giving of permission under Section 170 of MV Act,

Regarding the legal heirship of the petitioners is concerned Ex.P8 to Ex.P11, Ex.P13 to Ex.P15 Aadhar ID cards are produced.
Except these nothing is on record.
MVC in No 6195/2018 clubbed with this case came to be not pressed by the petitioners and petitioners in that case came to be impleaded in this case.

At the time of such impleadment there was no objection by the respondents is to be considered herein as the respondents are not much about the legal heirship as well as dependency of the petitioners are concerned.
Thus, the legal heirship and the dependency of petitioners stand established.

14. Wherefore, for the foregoing reasons, it establishes on preponderance of probability that Mr.
Mohammed Imran met with motor vehicle accident on 08.03.2018 at about 4.15 p.m., and sustained grievous injuries and died due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of car, bearing No.KA-51-ML-0963.
Hence, issue No.1 and 2 are answered affirmatively.

ISSUE No.3:
15.
In determination of this issue avocation, income, age of the deceased, dependency and future prospects and other conventional heads for compensation are need to be ascertained.
11 (SCCH-16) MVC 7880/2018 Avocation :
It is averred that the deceased was working as Plubming Contractor and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In substantiation of the same the petitioners have not produced any documents.
Hence, no other option but to consider notional income of the deceased in the present case.

Age: 
As per Ex.P13 - aadhar card, year of birth of the deceased was 1984 and so that age of the deceased was 34 years at the time of incident.
Hence, it is considered.
Income:
As discussed on the head of avocation, the deceased's avocation taken to be considered notionally.
In this regard as per the resolution of hon'ble the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, dated 17-02- 2022 notional income for the year 2018 came to be fixed at 12,500/.

In the present case, under the facts and circumstances of Mrs. M. Aasiya Tahseen vs Mr. Hitesh S on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135160327/
6 the case, Rs.12,500/- is taken to be considered as notional income of the deceased per month.

sentences.text: Personal and Living Expenses:
The legal heirship and dependency stood established.

6 petitioners are here, for deduction of personal expenses is concerned 1/4th is considered to 12 (SCCH-16)
MVC 7880/2018 be deducted in the monthly notional income of the deceased in his personal and living expenses.
Future prospects:

The future prospects is concerned, the age of the deceased at the time of the death was 34 years, so as per the principle laid down in Hem Raj vs. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others case, reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (SC), 40% needs to be added to the monthly notional income of the deceased.

entities.text: Hem Raj vs. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, 40% is added to the monthly income of the deceased.
Thus, 40% of addition will come to Rs.5,000/-.
In total, the monthly notional income will be Rs.17,500/-.
Conventional Heads:

As conventional heads, the deceased being husband of petitioner No.1 and 5 spousal consortium, father of petitioner No.2 and 6 parental consortium and son of petitioner No.3 and 4 filial consortium are to be considered as the petitioners suffered the loss of love and affection.

Hence, in view of the observations made, in the case of United India Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others, in civil Appeal No.2705/2020, by hon'ble the Apex Court, Rs.40,000/- each is considered to be awarded as compensation for consortium respectively.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd., vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The loss of estate is concerned, as the deceased was with the family, if the incident could not have been occurred, he could have been contributed more or less from his 13 (SCCH-16) MVC 7880/2018 savings to the estate of the family; the incident caused such loss to the estate of the petitioners.

Hence, Rs.15,000/- is need to be awarded on this head as the principle laid down by hon'ble the Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs.
Pranay Sethi, and others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

sentences.text: Likewise, for the funeral expenses is concerned awarding of Rs.15,000/- is also just under the conventional head as observed by hon'ble the Apex Court.
Hence, it is considered to be awarded.
16. Accordingly, compensation is calculated as under;
Monthly notional income of Rs.12,500/-.
Future prospects in 40% on the monthly notional income is Rs.5,000/-.
Monthly notional income + future prospects = 17,500/-.

sentences.text: For personal and living expenses, after the deduction of 1/4th, the total monthly notional income is Rs.13,125/-.
Net monthly notional income is Rs.13,125/- is calculated to net annul income as Rs.13,125/- x 12 which is = 1,57,500/-.
Multiplier is 16.
Net annual notional income is multiplied by multiplier 16, which is as Rs.1,57,500/- x 16, will come to Rs.25,20,000/-.
So, compensation for loss of dependency is found at Rs.25,20,000/- plus compensation on conventional heads, such as spousal, parental and filial consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.
18. Petitioners averred that they incurred Rs.4,00,000/- for the treatment of the deceased.
The medical records make it clear that before the death, the deceased had taken treatment in Apollo Hospital, Agadi Hospital and NIMHANS Hospital.
In proof of the same, they have produced 4 medical bills as per Ex.P12.
On careful examination it is seen that all the medical bills are genuine and there is no contra evidence to disbelieve the genuineness of these bills.
Hence, a sum of Rs.1,58,285/- is awarded under the head of medical expenses.

19. The details of compensation proposed to be awarded are as under:
 Sl. Head of  Amount/Rs  No. Compensation  1. Loss of dependency Rs. 25,20,000-00  2. Loss of spousal and Rs. 2,40,000-00  parental consortium
3 . Loss of estate Rs. 15,000-00  4. Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000-00  5.
Medical expenses Rs. 1,58,285-00  Total Rs. 29,48,285-00  15 (SCCH-16) MVC 7880/2018 20.
In all, petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.29,48,285/-, which can be rounded off to Rs.29,48,300/-.

Keeping in view the interest on the savings by the nationalized banks and as provided under Section 34 of the CPC, in the present case, from the date of petition only the interest at 6% per annum is considered to be directed till its realization.
So, the petitioners are entitled to the interest at 6% per annum on the compensation amount.

Liability:
21.
Insurance policy and its validity are admitted and no breaches are established by the insurer.
As found on the discussions on issue No.1, the negligence was on the part of the driver of the offended car.
On vicarious liability respondent No.1 being the owner is responsible, respondent No.2 being the insurer of respondent No.1 contractually liable to pay compensation.
Thus, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
However, initially respondent No.2 is liable to pay the determined compensation.
The petitioners are only entitled to such compensation and not fully as claimed for.
Accordingly, this issue stands answered partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE No.4:
22.
In view of the findings, the petition deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following order is passed:
16 (SCCH-16) MVC 7880/2018 ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

Petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.29,48,300/- (Rupees twenty nine lakhs, forty eight thousand and three hundred only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Compensation amount is  apportioned as follows:-
 Petitioner No.1 - Wife 30%
 Petitioner No.2 - Son 10%
 Petitioner No.3 - Father 10%
 Petitioner No.4 - Mother 10%
 Petitioner No.5 - Wife 30%
 Petitioner No.6 - Daughter 10%
 Out of the compensation amount awarded to petitioner No.1, and 5, 25% of the compensation amount with 17 (SCCH-16) MVC 7880/2018 proportionate interest shall be deposited in their names as FD in any nationalized bank for the period of two years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 75% amount with proportionate interest shall be released to them through E- payment on proper identification and verification.
The entire compensation amount amount with proportionate interest awarded to petitioner No.3 and 4 shall be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.

As conventional heads, the deceased being husband of petitioner No.1 and 5 spousal consortium, father of petitioner No.2 and 6 parental consortium and son of petitioner No.3 and 4 filial consortium are to be considered as the petitioners suffered the loss of love and affection.
The loss of estate is concerned, as the deceased was with the family, if the incident could not have been occurred, he could have been contributed more or less from his 13 (SCCH-16) MVC 7880/2018 savings to the estate of the family; the incident caused such loss to the estate of the petitioners.
Hence, Rs.15,000/- is need to be awarded on this head as the principle laid down by hon'ble the Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs.
Pranay Sethi, and others, reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.
Keeping in view the interest on the savings by the nationalized banks and as provided under Section 34 of the CPC, in the present case, from the date of petition only the interest at 6% per annum is considered to be directed till its realization.
As found on the discussions on issue No.1, the negligence was on the part of the driver of the offended car.
On vicarious liability respondent No.1 being the owner is responsible, respondent No.2 being the insurer of respondent No.1 contractually liable to pay compensation.
